subject: [PATCH v3 2/2] zstd: use cpu_feature_enabled() for in-kernel BMI2 dispatch

2026-09-01.patch_summary: This patch improves the performance of Zstandard (ZSTD) compression and decompression in the Linux kernel by using CPU feature checking to enable BMI2 dispatch, which is a hardware acceleration feature for x86 processors. The patch introduces two new macros, ZSTD_USE_BMI2() and ZSTD_SET_BMI2(), to control the use of BMI2 dispatch at runtime. It also updates various files to use these macros instead of relying on CPUID probing. This change allows the kernel to take advantage of hardware acceleration when available, resulting in significant performance improvements for compression and decompression operations.

reviews.author: Dhruva G
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Dhruva G noted that the patch does not handle the case where BMI2 is enabled but the CPUID-based dispatch is still used due to the x86 feature policy, and requested clarification on how this scenario is handled.

Reviewer Dhruva G pointed out that the comments in zstd_compress_internal.h and zstd_decompress_internal.h still indicate that BMI2 support is determined once per context, contradicting the changes made to use cpu_feature_enabled() for in-kernel BMI2 dispatch.

Reviewer noted that the patch does not include a necessary header file, <asm/cpufeature.h>, which is currently included separately by each .c user, and suggested including it in this header to avoid potential compilation issues.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Usama,

On 01-09-2026 16:37, Usama Arif wrote:

---

These comments still say BMI2 support is determined once per context:
- lib/zstd/compress/zstd_compress_internal.h:473
- lib/zstd/decompress/zstd_decompress_internal.h:159

---

Here, we do not include <asm/cpufeature.h>. Instead, every current .c user includes that header separately.
This works today, but it maybe fragile: the next user of ZSTD_USE_BMI2() can fail to compile unless they know
about this hidden requirement. 
Do you think perhaps we should provide that here in this header itself?

With that, feel free to add

Reviewed-by: Dhruva Gole <goledhruva@gmail.com>

2026-09-02.patch_summary: This patch improves the performance of Zstandard (ZSTD) compression and decompression in the Linux kernel by using CPU feature checks to enable BMI2 instructions at runtime, rather than relying on static CPUID probing. The patch introduces a new abstraction for context initialization and uses x86 feature policy to allow x86 alternatives to resolve feature checks at boot time. This change improves performance by reducing the number of branches and allowing the CPU to optimize instruction sequences. Benchmarks show a 19.5% reduction in compression time and a 72.3% reduction in decompression time.
